tasks.short: Decide the patient is ready for discharge, arrange follow-up and home care, prepare the discharge medication list, and explain the discharge plan.

steps.what: Hospitalist conducts discharge planning and decides the patient is ready
Hospitalist arranges follow-up care and home care by phone
Hospitalist prepares the discharge medication list
Hospitalist explains the discharge plan and discharges patients

tasks.design: A discharge checklist in the record ({OTHER}) sends structured transfer requests to home care and follow-up clinics through the regional transfer system, so most arrangements no longer need phone calls. The discharge medication list starts from the inpatient orders and the admission list, and the hospitalist reconciles the differences. Deciding on discharge and explaining the plan stay with the hospitalist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Follow-up care was arranged by phone and medication lists rebuilt by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records send transfer requests and reconcile medication lists.
tasks.still_hard: Nursing home places still need calls.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a patient will not cope at home yet.

evidence.claim: Records can send structured transfer requests and reconcile medication lists.
The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ward round to the patient discharged; care after discharge is outside.
Input contract: home care providers on the transfer system; fallback is phone.
Discharge decisions stay with the hospitalist.
Home care staff read transfers as they took calls.

incremental.description: Hospitalist chases transfer requests without a reply.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex discharges to nursing homes; high: routine discharges home.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather the hospital course, results and medication, write the discharge summary, code the diagnoses, check the summary, and send it to the GP.

steps.what: Hospitalist gathers the hospital course, results and medication from the record

loop.input: The admission notes, daily notes, results and medication changes in the record.
loop.output: A draft narrative of the hospital course and the plan for the GP.
loop.check: A validator flags any diagnosis, medication, dose or result not in the record; the hospitalist edits every summary.
loop.stop: One draft per discharge; if rejected, the hospitalist writes the narrative.
loop.why_not_simpler: The hospital course is spread over many free-text notes; a template cannot condense it.

steps.what: Hospitalist codes the diagnoses for the summary

loop.input: The draft summary and the problem list.
loop.output: Suggested ICD-10 and SNOMED codes per diagnosis.
loop.check: Each suggested code must exist in the code set and match a diagnosis named in the summary; the hospitalist confirms every code.
loop.stop: One pass per summary; diagnoses without a suggestion are coded by the hospitalist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Diagnoses are written in free text; a lookup by keyword misses most of them.

steps.what: Hospitalist checks the final discharge summary
Hospitalist sends discharge summaries to primary care physicians

tasks.design: The discharge summary template in the record ({OTHER}) fills admission reason, results, procedures and medication changes from structured data. A bounded step drafts the narrative of the hospital course from the notes; a validator flags any diagnosis, medication or result not in the record, and the hospitalist edits every summary. Suggested codes are confirmed one by one. Once checked, the summary goes to the GP through secure messaging.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts were copied from many screens and the narrative written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical tools draft letters and suggest codes; records fill templates.
tasks.still_hard: Long admissions have many conflicting notes.
tasks.human_edge: Telling the GP the one thing to watch this week.
tasks.altitude: The hospitalist edits summaries instead of compiling them.

reach.learn: Whether summaries arrive on discharge day.

evidence.claim: Juvoly drafts referral letters and suggests ICPC, ICD-10 and SNOMED codes.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry MDR class IIa.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient discharged to the summary sent; the GP's follow-up is outside.
Input contract: structured data in the record; fallback is copying by hand.
The hospitalist edits every summary and confirms every code.
research_questions: Do summaries reach the GP on discharge day more often?

incremental.description: Hospitalist reports wrong drafts and codes to the system team.

approvals.approved_version: The summary as checked by the hospitalist in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: long complex admissions; high: short routine admissions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead ward rounds directing nurses and support staff, write orders and tasks, answer nurses' calls for clarification, and hand over at shift change.

steps.what: Hospitalist directs patient care activities of nursing staff on ward rounds
Hospitalist writes orders and tasks for nurses as free text
Hospitalist answers nurses' calls to clarify orders
Hospitalist hands over patients at shift change

tasks.design: Orders and nursing tasks use order sets with fixed fields (what, when, until when, call if) in the record ({OTHER}), so orders are clearer and fewer calls are needed to clarify them. The handover uses a structured list from the record with open tasks and patients to watch. Directing staff on rounds stays with the hospitalist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were written as free text and handovers prepared from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Records hold order sets and structured handover lists.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing which nurse's worry needs a bedside visit now.

evidence.claim: Records can hold order sets with fixed fields and structured handover lists.
Systems that log who did what can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ward round to the shift handed over; nursing care is outside.
Input contract: order sets set up; fallback is free text.
Nurses read structured orders in about the time free text took.

incremental.description: Hospitalist adds notes when no order set fits.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small wards; high: large wards with many orders.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive the consultation request, review the patient's record, examine the patient, advise the treating team, and write the consult note.

steps.what: Hospitalist receives inpatient consultation requests by phone
Hospitalist attends inpatient consultations and examines the patient

tasks.design: Consultations are requested electronically in the record ({OTHER}) with a structured question and urgency, so routine requests do not come by phone. The consult view shows problems, medication, recent results and the question together. The consult note uses a template that starts from the question. Examining and advising stay with the hospitalist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by phone without a clear question, and data were gathered from several screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Records support electronic consult requests and summary views.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent consults still come by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the finding the treating team missed.

evidence.claim: Records can carry electronic consult requests with structured questions and summary views.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consult request to the consult note; follow-up care is outside.
Input contract: requesting teams use the electronic request; fallback is phone.
Requesting doctors fill the request in about the time a call took.
research_questions: Do consults happen sooner after the request?

incremental.description: Hospitalist asks for clarification on vague requests.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly urgent consults; high: mostly planned consults.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The hospitalist keeps deciding discharges, directing care, examining and advising; phone arrangements, compiled summaries, free-text orders and phone consult requests shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A hospitalist with more time at the bedside.
